items.proposed_content: The strengthened two-sided oscillation bounds show that the empirically persistent inequality between the prime count and the logarithmic integral must eventually fail. The source explains the long finite-range bias by competition between a slowly varying fixed-sign term and a larger oscillatory term whose extra triple-logarithmic factor grows extraordinarily slowly. It records dependence on Kronecker's Diophantine-approximation theorems and extends analogous two-sided behavior to a weighted prime sum and the two odd residue classes modulo four. Thus asymptotic dominance need not be computationally visible, and the optimal growth factor remains open.

items.proposed_content: The unit establishes a one-way conditional result: Tschebyschef's divergence assertion for an alternating prime exponential sum follows if every complex zero of the displayed Dirichlet L-function lies on the critical line. The authors expect failure of the assertion when that zero condition fails but explicitly do not prove it. Interpreting the alternating weights as competition between prime residue classes and the L-function as its analytic proxy is useful, provided it is not promoted into an equivalence or an unstated transform argument.

items.proposed_content: A contour contribution is reduced to oscillatory Dirichlet integrals whose phase has nonstationary tails and at most one stationary central index. Bounds for the tails and a local quadratic expansion at resonance give the uniform cancellation estimate, and the critical-line sign-change argument later reuses exactly this phase decomposition to control its horizontal integral.

items.proposed_content: For the arithmetic errors treated here, exponential and positive-order Riesz or Cesaro smoothing expose zero-controlled square-root-scale behavior that the sharp summatory function need not share. The source also shows that transfer is directional: upper and lower results pass between smoothing schemes in different directions, and preserving a one-sided prime-counting oscillation requires an additional Cesaro-controlled remainder.

items.proposed_content: The critical-line zero lower bound is built from a local sign-change mechanism: a real auxiliary function is shown to have a small integral on each prescribed short interval, while constant sign would identify that integral with an absolute-value integral whose functional-equation and Dirichlet-series evaluation has a larger main term. Hence every sufficiently high interval contains an odd-order zero, and counting such intervals gives the global lower bound.

items.proposed_content: The source first computes a large seed value as the analytic boundary is approached, then reproduces it arbitrarily high in the strip by truncating the zero expansion, controlling its tail, and simultaneously aligning the finitely many remaining phases. A boundary-growth principle transfers the resulting interior extremes to the boundary function, and the explicit arithmetic formula turns them into recurring prime-counting oscillations.

items.proposed_content: The source turns the gap in a Ramanujan-inspired reciprocal formula into a precise contour-shift obligation: horizontal boundary integrals must vanish along suitable heights. It then generalizes the reciprocal-transform setup but keeps those formulas conjectural, while separately deriving and proving a Riesz-growth condition equivalent to RH.

items.proposed_content: The source separates two superficially similar spectral intuitions by their missing proof obligations. Under RH, a lowest conjugate zero pair yields signed oscillation only after the remaining zero tail is quantitatively dominated; by contrast, the expectation that an off-line Dirichlet-L zero destroys the conditional residue-class bias remains heuristic because larger spectral size has not been converted into controlled sign and remainder behavior.

items.proposed_content: The source separates three proof interfaces: analytic continuation determines where a Mellin contour may move, the kernel supplies smoothing and vertical decay, and independent coefficient conditions license Tauberian recovery. Boundary regularity and a simple pole change the contour contribution, while replacing the exponential kernel by a fractional-power kernel removes an artificial vertical-growth cutoff without changing the intended partial-sum conclusion.

items.proposed_content: The zeta-based centered von Mangoldt error and the Dirichlet-L residue-class bias follow a shared explicit-formula architecture: Mellin inversion and contour displacement replace coefficient sums by nontrivial-zero terms plus controlled corrections, after which separate spectral bounds and coefficient decompositions identify the arithmetic contribution that governs the conclusion.
